clf-med-066.text: An industry needs to connect its data center on-premises to AWS. The operation requires consistent bandwidth, predictable and stable latency for large daily data transfers, and the company accepts a period of weeks for provisioning. AWS Site-to-Site VPN and AWS Direct Connect, which option answers best and why?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN because dedicated connections cannot support large data transfers
AWS Site-to-Site VPN because it provides the highest guaranteed bandwidth in the AWS connectivity portfolio
AWS Direct Connect because it provides dedicated private connectivity with more consistent network performance than internet-based VPN connectivity
AWS Direct Connect because it is provisioned instantly with no physical dependencies
clf-med-066.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between a customer location and AWS and is designed for workloads that benefit from more consistent bandwidth and latency than internet-based connectivity, although provisioning can take longer.
clf-med-066.hint: Compare encrypted connectivity over the public internet with a dedicated network connection. Which one is designed for consistency at large sustained volumes?
optionRationales: AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between a customer location and AWS and is designed for workloads that benefit from more consistent bandwidth and latency than internet-based connectivity, although provisioning can take longer.
Site-to-Site VPN uses encrypted tunnels over internet connectivity and therefore remains subject to internet-path variability, even though it can be provisioned more quickly.
AWS Direct Connect is specifically used for dedicated high-capacity connectivity and large regular data transfers, so the statement that it cannot support large transfers is incorrect.
AWS Direct Connect can involve physical circuit provisioning and is not generally an instant no-dependency connectivity option.

clf-med-067.text: A news portal uses Amazon RDS and experiences slowdowns during traffic peaks because readers generate a very large number of read queries while writes are relatively infrequent. The team wants to scale READ capacity without changing the primary database instance. Which RDS feature addresses this requirement?
options: Increase provisioned storage on the instance
clf-med-067.explanation: RDS Read Replicas are asynchronous replicas that can serve read traffic and help scale read-heavy workloads horizontally without placing all read queries on the primary database instance.
clf-med-067.hint: Differentiate the two common RDS concepts: one primarily supports high availability and failover; the other scales read queries.
optionRationales: RDS Read Replicas are asynchronous replicas that can serve read traffic and help scale read-heavy workloads horizontally without placing all read queries on the primary database instance.
A standard Multi-AZ standby is primarily designed for high availability and automatic failover rather than serving application read traffic.
Snapshots are point-in-time backup artifacts used for recovery and do not distribute live query load.
Increasing storage capacity increases available database storage but does not directly add independent read-processing endpoints.

clf-med-068.text: A fintech company needs a relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL but wants a cloud-native architecture with high throughput, distributed auto-growing storage, and multiple copies of data across three Availability Zones. Which AWS database service was designed specifically for these characteristics?
clf-med-068.explanation: The Aurora is the relational bank of AWS compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, designed for cloud performance up to 5x (MySQL) and 3x (PostgreSQL) top, self-scalable storage and six copies of data distributed in three AZs.
clf-med-068.hint: Think of AWS's cloud-native relational database known for compatibility with both MySQL and PostgreSQL and a distributed multi-AZ storage layer.
optionRationales: The Aurora is the relational bank of AWS compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, designed for cloud performance up to 5x (MySQL) and 3x (PostgreSQL) top, self-scalable storage and six copies of data distributed in three AZs.
Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value and document database and is not MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible.
Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse optimized for analytics rather than a transactional MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational database.
Amazon Neptune is a graph database for highly connected datasets and does not provide MySQL or PostgreSQL compatibility.

clf-med-069.text: A retail BI team needs to run complex analytical SQL queries, aggregations, joins, and historical reports over petabytes of structured sales data using standard SQL and business-intelligence tools. Which AWS service is the appropriate managed data warehouse for this analytical workload?
clf-med-069.explanation: Amazon Redshift is AWS's managed data warehouse designed for large-scale analytical workloads and integrates with SQL-based analytics and business-intelligence tools.
clf-med-069.hint: Petabytes plus SQL plus BI reporting points to the data-warehouse category. Identify the AWS service in that category.
optionRationales: Amazon Redshift is AWS's managed data warehouse designed for large-scale analytical workloads and integrates with SQL-based analytics and business-intelligence tools.
Amazon RDS is primarily optimized for transactional relational workloads rather than petabyte-scale analytical warehousing.
Amazon DynamoDB excels at low-latency NoSQL access patterns and is not designed for relational joins and large ad hoc analytical SQL queries.
Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache used to accelerate applications and is not a persistent analytical data warehouse.

clf-med-070.text: A recipe website repeatedly runs the same database queries, such as the day's most popular recipes, and unnecessarily overloads Amazon RDS. The architect wants an in-memory cache layer compatible with Redis or Memcached to serve repeated reads with very low latency and reduce database load. Which managed AWS service provides this layer?
clf-med-070.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache is AWS's managed in-memory caching service and supports engines designed for high-speed caching workloads such as Redis-compatible and Memcached environments.
clf-med-070.hint: The Redis and Memcached names point directly to AWS's managed in-memory cache service.
optionRationales: Amazon ElastiCache is AWS's managed in-memory caching service and supports engines designed for high-speed caching workloads such as Redis-compatible and Memcached environments.
DAX is an in-memory cache specifically designed for DynamoDB rather than a general cache layer for relational databases such as RDS.
Amazon CloudFront caches web content at edge locations for end users rather than database query results between an application and its database.
Amazon EFS is a shared elastic file system and is not a sub-millisecond in-memory database cache.
